stories.headline: Russia and US seek to block plan for binding rules on autonomous weapons
stories.script: Our lead story today. UN conference this month seen as key moment after years of discussions on filling gap in governance of AI systems Plans to fill a gap in the global governance of autonomous weapons are in jeopardy as a group of nations led by Russia and the US move to use a UN conference this month to block proposals to negotiate a legally binding set of rules. The scale of the opposition will become clear at a diplomatic retreat starting on Friday before the seventh review conference on “certain conventional weapons” in Geneva due to be attended by 128 countries from 16 to 20 November.

stories.headline: Google sued over suicide-related AI chats on school computer
stories.script: Turning to the United States. The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT.

stories.headline: Nigel Farage's exit from the Telegraph may be cause for cheer. But there’s a sobering side to this story | Jane Martinson
stories.script: Around the world. The clear-out at the newspaper seems driven less by politics than by a shift towards AI and journalism will pay the price Nigel Farage has been writing columns for the Daily Telegraph since 2016 , most of which have promoted the previously Brexit and now Reform UK party he leads, or accused his rivals of going soft on immigration . For this privilege the paper’s cash-strapped bosses paid him around £4,000 a month , adding up to nearly half a million pounds over the past decade. News broke this week that Farage’s services are no longer required by the Telegraph’s new German owners, Axel Springer, though sources close to Farage say that he resigned.
